articles.title: 曝微软曾向 Netflix 开价 8 亿美元，寻求 XBOX 游戏 7 年独家影视改编权
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，当地时间 23 日，外媒 Puck 援引三名知情人士消息称，微软曾向 Netflix 开价 8 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 53.51 亿元人民币），希望达成为期 7 年的独家授权协议，允许 Netflix 将 XBOX 旗下游戏角色改编成电影和剧集，并在其流媒体平台上独家播出。Netflix 最初为获得 XBOX 游戏的影视独家改编授权提出 5 亿美元（现汇率约合 33.44 亿元人民币）的报价，授权期限为 7 年。但微软要求将价格提高至 8 亿美元，双方最终未能谈成。XBOX 对此回应：“外界对我们旗下游戏知识产权的合作兴趣达到创纪录水平。Netflix 是我们重视的合作伙伴，双方合作的《我的世界》和《暗黑破坏神》动画剧集即将推出，我们对此十分期待。此外，双方还有其他改编作品。”Netflix 拒绝对此置评。据报道，XBOX 转而寻求与更多合作伙伴达成规模较小的交易，不再争取一揽子独家授权协议。微软此前曾与派拉蒙合作推出《光环》真人剧集。该剧于 2022 年首播，第二季于 2024 年 2 月上线，随后在同年 7 月被取消。Netflix 则与多家游戏开发商合作，推出了多部热门改编作品。其中包括动画《赛博朋克：边缘行者》，其第二季已于本周上线。知名游戏制作人小岛秀夫在新一季动画中客串出演，此前他也曾在《赛博朋克 2077》中客串登场。

articles.title: 苹果推送 iOS 27.1 更新，其首款折叠 iPhone Duo 独享
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，科技媒体 MacRumors 昨日（10 月 23 日）发布博文，报道称苹果公司针对其首款折叠 iPhone Duo，推送仅限于该机型的 iOS 27.1 更新，在官方日志中仅显示“修复 iPhone 上的错误”。原文并未提及本次推送的内部版本号，只是提及苹果公司已于本周四以 IPSW 文件的形式提供下载，在下载链接中显示版本号为 24A94425。不过IT之家查询社交媒体平台，开发者 @aaronp613 反馈该版本于 10 月 14 日推送，而苹果公司于 10 月 20 日还推送了 24B91016 版本。更新内容方面，这次更新的内容相当低调，苹果仅表示“修复 iPhone 上的错误”，没有披露具体细节，也未包含任何安全修复。外界普遍认为，苹果将 iOS 27.1 独占给 iPhone Duo，主要是为了在折叠屏手机正式发售前，避免 Duo 专属的软件功能、界面适配或系统架构提前泄露。由于 iPhone Duo 采用全新折叠形态，其系统需要针对外屏、内屏、分屏、横屏应用等场景进行专门优化，苹果或许不希望这些细节过早出现在其他机型的测试版中。

articles.title: 谷歌 CEO 皮查伊：距离 AI 能自我改进的“最终状态”，我们还有很长的路要走
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，据《商业内幕》报道，谷歌 CEO 桑达尔 · 皮查伊认为，距离 AI 能够完全自主地改进自身，还有很长的路要走。皮查伊透露，谷歌研究人员开始使用 AI 智能体辅助开发模型，但技术仍处于起步阶段。“我们距离递归自我改进（RSI）的最终形态还很远。准确地说，在模型研发的各个环节，AI 研究人员已经开始与自我改进循环协同工作。可以说，AI 智能体正以一定程度的自动化方式协助研究人员，共同开发模型。”皮查伊预计，明年还将看到进一步进展。谷歌联合创始人谢尔盖 · 布林本月早些时候曾谈到，公司的 Flash 系列模型和 Gemini 4 已展现出 AI 参与自身研发的能力。目前，研究人员正与 AI 模型携手开发下一代模型。IT之家从报道中获悉，今年 4 月，谷歌曾披露内部新增代码已有 75% 由 AI 生成。但在皮查伊看来，单纯统计 AI 生成代码的比例已无法准确反映实际情况。“对我们来说，这个数字已经没什么意义，因为现在经我们处理的每一段代码，都受到 AI 的深刻影响。”皮查伊还提到，Gemini 4 Argon 将帮助人们处理更复杂的编程难题。谷歌因程序错误或系统故障而将软件恢复至旧版本的次数，也减少了三分之一。“因此我认为，AI 工具不仅提高了编程效率，也改善了代码质量。”

articles.title: OpenAI 为前沿 AI 训练 / 评估开启“断网闭关”模式，遏制其越狱攻击
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，OpenAI 昨日（10 月 23 日）发布博文，宣布针对最先进“前沿模型”的训练与评估环境，已经实施更严格的安全管控，明确在模型训练期间，不得直接访问实时互联网。该公司称出于对 AI 安全的负责任要求，基于当前对齐研究、监测能力和互联网基础设施安全状况做出的决策，相关限制将持续到安全防护取得足够进展为止。OpenAI 的一款内部研究模型于 9 月 20 日利用 DNS 配置漏洞，在训练过程中短暂获得有限的互联网访问权限，因此该公司于 9 月还一度暂停训练与评估前沿模型。OpenAI 随后加强了研究环境隔离、缩小智能体可利用的攻击面，并改进了异常行为检测与自动停止机制，于 10 月 1 日恢复强化学习训练及内部推理。为避免模型接触真实网络，OpenAI 构建了一个“离线世界”：由大量已索引和缓存的网页内容组成，供模型在封闭环境中练习浏览、使用工具和执行代码等任务。IT之家附上相关截图如下：智能体仍可使用浏览器、计算机操作工具和代码环境，但只能访问与实时互联网隔离的安全环境；未经授权的智能体之间通信也受到限制。OpenAI 表示，随着 AI 智能体能力增强，其未来可能发现并利用当前尚未被识别的软件漏洞，因此必须在训练阶段切断其对外部系统的潜在影响。OpenAI 表示将在受控、离线的沙箱中推进前沿模型研发，同时继续测试虚拟机、隔离机制和监测系统的薄弱环节。

articles.title: 支付宝官宣适配 iPhone Duo 全场景，支持页面布局自动调整等特性
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，支付宝官方昨晚发文宣布，已适配 iPhone Duo。据介绍，在 iPhone Duo 上升级支付宝 App 至最新 12.12.38 版本支持如下功能：1、底部栏：液态玻璃效果，界面通透，展示新体验。2、适配全场景：内屏外屏、横屏竖屏等各种使用方式，页面布局自动调整。支付宝官方表示：“支付宝适配 iPhone Duo 的每一种生活姿态：展开，生活尽收眼底；折起，钱包随身而行。”关于更多 iPhone Duo 的最新消息，小伙伴们可以参考IT之家的首发上手体验视频了解更多。点击关注IT之家B站账号延伸阅读iPhone Duo 是苹果推出的首款折叠屏手机，采用书本式折叠设计，配备 7.6 英寸可折叠内屏和 5.4 英寸外屏，均采用超视网膜 XDR 显示屏并支持 ProMotion 自适应刷新率技术。该机搭载 A20 Pro 芯片，支持硬件加速光线追踪，后置 4800 万像素融合式主摄与 4800 万像素融合式超广角镜头，支持最高 4K、120 帧杜比视界视频拍摄；同时没有实体 SIM 卡槽，仅支持 eSIM。iPhone Duo 于 2026 年 10 月 23 日正式开售，国行起售价为 15999 元，是苹果史上最贵的 iPhone，苹果中国官网显示每位顾客限购 2 部。苹果官方数据显示，该机使用外屏播放视频最长可达 44 小时，使用内屏播放视频最长可达 31 小时。文中提到的“液态玻璃”对应的是苹果在 iOS 26 中引入的 Liquid Glass 设计语言，被视为自 iOS 7 以来最大的设计更新，为锁定屏幕、主屏幕、控制中心和 App 带来全新设计，系统内的各种 UI 按钮也围绕液态玻璃和圆角设计，可折射光线并通过镜面高光动态响应用户的操作。

articles.title: “行为难以预测”存在安全隐患，OpenAI 将不再在实时互联网上训练模型
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，当地时间 23 日，OpenAI 宣布，今后将使用缓存的网页内容和模拟互联网环境训练模型，不再让模型直接接入真实互联网。公司认为，模型的行为仍然难以预测，直接赋予联网权限存在安全隐患。竞争对手 Anthropic 两周前也开始限制旗下最新、理论上能力最强的模型直接联网。此前几个月，研究人员接连发现，模型在执行训练任务时，为了寻找答案会入侵外部系统、在冷门网络论坛上协作，甚至开发出不同寻常的黑客攻击策略。接连发生的事件促使两家实验室收紧模型的联网权限。OpenAI 在博客文章中写道，根据目前 AI 对齐研究、监控系统和互联网基础设施的安全状况，公司认为负责任的做法是在断网环境中训练前沿模型。OpenAI 披露，直到 9 月 20 日，公司仍有一款前沿模型利用系统配置失误接入互联网。随后，OpenAI 暂停了 9 月余下时间的训练工作，转而开发和测试新的安全防护方案。改用断网沙箱训练模型，与前沿 AI 实验室员工此前的判断形成反差。他们过去一直强调，要在完全隔离互联网的环境中开展模型训练，实际操作起来几乎行不通。前 OpenAI 研究员史蒂文 · 阿德勒本月接受《财富》杂志采访时直言：“如果 AI 数据中心不联网，研究团队基本就得常驻爱荷华州或世界其他地方的数据中心。额外负担会非常大。如果一家企业独自承担如此高的代价，换来的安全收益是否足够大、值不值得，我没有把握。”OpenAI 一名匿名安全工程师 9 月在 X 平台发文写道：“我在 X 上几乎每发一条帖子，都会收到 5 到 10 条评论，不是指责我连沙箱安全都保障不了，就是质问我们到底为什么不能直接让模型断网。评论反映出，许多组织和个人的认识，与前沿 AI 实验室实际面临的问题之间，差距越来越大。人们对实验室如何训练和评估模型也普遍存在误解。”此次，OpenAI 则强调：“我们必须始终有能力阻止前沿模型未经授权、随意接入真实互联网。”此前，公司曾在红队测试中让大批 AI 智能体尝试突破沙箱限制。测试暴露出一系列安全漏洞，最终促使 OpenAI 改变模型训练方式。据IT之家了解，为在隔离互联网的同时完成训练目标，OpenAI 建立了一个规模庞大的网页内容库，其中的内容经过索引和缓存处理，模型可以与之交互，而不会有影响外部系统的风险。断网训练能否达到让模型自由访问开放互联网时的效果，还有待验证。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，小米创办人、董事长兼 CEO 雷军昨日转发了小米集团副总裁、汽车部 CTO 胡峥楠的微博，并宣布小米纽北 Workshop 已经启用。据胡峥楠介绍，小米在纽北刚启用不久的 Workshop 位于 GT 赛道旁，比之前租用附近的 Workshop 面积大了不少，设施也完全鸟枪换炮，员工的办公工作条件也大为改善，有了自己的停车场、快充站、进入赛道的专用入口、给车手的浴室等，最意外的是还有专属的观赛 VIP Lounge。IT之家注意到，在胡峥楠分享的照片中，还出现了一款与 SU7 Ultra 外观相似的神秘新车，目前还贴有伪装车衣，预计就是全新一代的小米 SU7 Ultra。今年 9 月，多位博主分享了小米新款 SU7 Ultra 国内测试车谍照。画面显示，新车采用了超大尾翼设计。另外，侧视图揭露了车门设计的一角，新车或采用双门方案。还有消息称这款车型将采用限量版形式推出，或命名为 SU7 Ultra Extreme，并配备多项醒目的空气动力学部件，拥有巨大的后扰流板，以及采用大型鳍片、用于减少气流扰动的后扩散器。

articles.title: 美国宇航局调整载人登月方案：SpaceX 星舰改在地球附近对接，蓝色起源减少加注环节
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，科技媒体 Ars Technica 今天（10 月 24 日）发布博文，报道称在当地时间 23 日周五举办的新闻发布会上，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）公布“阿耳忒弥斯”（Artemis）登月计划调整方案，仍争取于 2027 年夏季开展近地对接演示，并在 2028 年通过“阿耳忒弥斯 4 号”（Artemis 4）任务实现载人登月。IT之家援引博文介绍，本次“阿耳忒弥斯”登月计划任务调整的核心是“减负”，美国宇航局不再要求 SpaceX 和蓝色起源两家登月器供应商严格遵循同一套会合路线，通过分别修改两家供应商的任务流程，争取让“阿耳忒弥斯 3 号”在 2027 年先完成地球轨道测试，再由“阿耳忒弥斯 4 号”于 2028 年尝试载人登月。针对 SpaceX 的星舰方案，美国宇航局调整“猎户座”载人飞船与星舰登月器的对接地点。在此前的方案中，星舰需要前往月球附近的“近直线晕轨道”，在那里与“猎户座”会合。按照新方案，两者改在高地球轨道对接，然后再前往月球。星舰月球着陆器运行概念图。图源：NASA报道指出，原来的月球轨道对接要求会增加星舰的能量需求，并带来其他任务困难。但改变会合地点，并没有取消星舰在地球轨道补充推进剂的需求。SpaceX 仍需通过储存推进剂的飞行器和多次加注飞行，为登月器提供足够燃料。蓝色起源方面，“蓝月亮”（Blue Moon）登月器采取另一条路线：新版任务架构包括四次“新格伦”火箭发射，但不需要飞行器之间进行推进剂转移。“蓝月亮”月球着陆器运行概念图。图源：NASA本次调整后拆分任务设计与“在太空中给另一艘飞船加注”这一技术环节。作为对照，星舰方案仍依赖在轨推进剂转移，因此两家公司面临的技术路径和风险并不相同。此外，新方案允许“蓝月亮”与“猎户座”在低月球轨道会合。与此同时，NASA 正与联合发射联盟合作开发加长版“半人马座 V”上面级，计划配合太空发射系统火箭，让“猎户座”能够抵达低月球轨道。这有望降低“蓝月亮”往返月面的燃料需求，并增加紧急撤离机会。不过，相关能力仍待开发，2028 年登月目前仍是目标，而非确定结果。美国宇航局正致力于研发和改进半人马座 5 号上面级，以便将猎户座飞船送入近月轨道。图源：美国宇航局

articles.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro 正式发布：月之暗面最强 3 万亿级模型，编程智能体测评超 GPT-6
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，今天（24 日）凌晨，月之暗面 Kimi 宣布正式推出 Kimi K3.1 系列的第一个模型 ——K3.1 Pro，也是公司迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。高速版模型 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 同步推出，同等智能，输出速度约 2~3 倍。即日起，用户可通过 kimi.com、Kimi App、Kimi Work、Kimi Code 和 Kimi API (platform.kimi.com)，使用 Kimi K3.1 Pro 和 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 模型。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。IT之家从官方介绍获悉，在代码、Agent 和知识类基准上，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强闭源模型的水平。Terminal-Bench 4.0 通过真实环境中资源受限的终端任务考察编程智能体的能力，每项任务均设有严格的专项测试。K3.1 Pro 在此项评估中得分 65.7%，超过 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅有微弱差距。Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 则是内部的基准测试，覆盖多种工程领域，重点考察编程智能体的多步执行、工具调用和端到端问题解决能力。K3.1 Pro 在这项测试中得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。K3.1 Pro 能熟练使用 Unity、Unreal Engine、Godot 等游戏引擎，并结合网络搜索与 3D 生成，做出完整的体验。它产出的前端页面、Three.js 交互场景和 3D 资产，在构图、排版、动效和细节打磨上都有明显提升。Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型擅长 3D 创作与空间推理。在 BenchCAD 基准测试中，K3.1 Pro 借助工具得分 92.7%，接近 Claude Opus 5.5 的 96.2% 和 GPT-6 Astra 的 95.9%。该基准考察通过生成 CAD 代码，从多视角渲染图重建 3D 模型的能力。据介绍，给 K3.1 Pro 一段文字描述、一张草图或一张参考图，它能推断出物体的形状、比例和空间关系，并将其重建为可用的 3D 模型。它对现有素材库和模型库也有更强的理解。K3.1 Pro 擅长参数化建模，例如机械零件、建筑模型、多参数可配置的产品和定制家具。无需依赖 MCP 连接器，它可以直接编写并运行 Blender、CAD 等专业建模工具的脚本，完成素材的构建与细化，修改单个部件，并调整几何、材质与场景布局。kimi.com 和 Kimi app 已同步上线 3D Make 功能，支持在线预览和编辑 3D 模型，做好的模型可以直接下载去 3D 打印，也能导出视频或实况照片，随手分享到社交平台。Kimi K3.1 Pro 还能够端到端交付完整的金融工作流。在外部基准上，K3.1 Pro 在 OfficeQA Pro v2 基准测试中得分 64.4，取得当前最优成绩（SoTA）。OfficeQA Pro v2 考察基于真实金融文档的复杂财务数据分析，涉及检索、跨文档核对与多步数值推理。K3.1 Pro 在 Frontier Finance 上的表现也较 K3 进一步提升。该基准测试衡量模型对完整投资工作流的支持能力，覆盖从标的筛选到盈利分析的全过程。在 3 个内部金融基准上，K3.1 Pro 同样全面超过 K3：财务建模基准 Financial Modelling 考察真实建模任务中的公式联动、财务逻辑与最终工作簿质量，K3.1 Pro 较 K3 提高 14%。金融研究基准 Financial Research 用于检验模型能否完成真实场景下的金融研究工作，并在证据与截止条件约束下输出可核验的结果。K3.1 为较 K3 提升 20%。商业运营基准 Business Operation 在模拟商业环境中考察长程经营管理与决策能力，K3.1 Pro 得分约为 K3 的 4.2 倍。在专门针对事实准确性开展的内部压力测试 Kimi Hallu Bench Hard 中，新模型的单项事实陈述错误率从 K3 的 23.4% 降至 8.3%；包含至少一处事实错误的回答比例仅为前代的约 42.4%。（这是一项针对事实准确性的压力测试，样本刻意聚焦模型容易出错的情形，所报告的错误率不代表日常使用中的整体水平。）接入 Kimi API 开发应用：访问 Kimi 开放平台（platform.kimi.com），模型选择 kimi-k3.1-pro，价格为每百万 Token 输入：1.3 元（命中缓存）和  13 元（未命中缓存），输出 68  元。高速版模型 kim

articles.title: 32GB 内存可“任性”关闭 Win11 分页文件？微软给出最终答案
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 昨日（10 月 23 日）发布博文，围绕“32GB 内存电脑是否还需要分页文件”话题，基于微软相关支持文档表述，认为分页文件的大小应结合实际负载与崩溃转储需求确定，不能仅凭内存容量一刀切。IT之家援引博文介绍，分页文件是 Windows 放在硬盘或 SSD 上的一种隐藏系统文件，通常叫 pagefile.sys，可视为内存的后备空间。程序运行时，需要把正在处理的数据放进内存。Windows 会以“页”为单位管理这些数据，“分页文件”的名称也由此而来。系统可以将不常访问、已被修改的内存页写入分页文件，等程序再次需要时，再调回物理内存。例如用户同时打开游戏、浏览器和办公软件，某个后台程序里暂时用不到的数据，就可能被移到分页文件中。不过，分页文件并非只有在“内存彻底用满”后才会发挥作用，Windows 会根据内存管理需要进行调度。此外分页文件还能扩大系统可支持的“已提交内存”（系统向程序承诺提供的内存总量上限）上限。关闭分页文件后，就会降低这个上限；一旦程序申请的总量触及上限，可能出现内存分配失败、程序崩溃或系统卡顿。报道举例称，作者一台 32GB 内存电脑的实际内存占用为 24.7GB，已提交内存却达到 39.2GB。关闭分页文件后，提交上限会降至略低于物理内存容量；一旦触及上限，即使看起来仍有空闲内存，程序也可能无法继续申请内存，出现卡顿或崩溃。此外，在未配置专用转储文件的情况下，禁用页面文件还可能影响系统保存崩溃转储，增加排查故障的难度。至于“关闭后游戏更快”，报道指出，内存需求本就不高时，禁用它通常没有多少性能收益，却会削弱多任务场景下的缓冲能力。对于普通用户，该媒体基于微软官方指导推荐，认为用户不必因为装了 32GB 内存就关闭分页文件，也不要机械套用“必须设为内存的 1.5 倍”之类固定公式，推荐保留 Windows 默认的“自动管理所有磁盘的分页文件大小”。系统管理模式会根据需求调整大小，但需要磁盘留有可用空间。需要注意的是，分页文件主要提供容量余地，而不是让电脑凭空提速。如果日常负载长期超过物理内存承受范围，增大分页文件并不能等价替代升级内存。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 24 日消息，安全公司 Calif.io 昨日（10 月 23 日）在 X 平台发布推文，分享了一段演示视频，在苹果首款折叠 iPhone Duo 开售首日，便成功在 iOS 27.1 系统上实现越狱。为了演示本次越狱成果，Calif 实现了不同于常规系统的界面效果，屏幕右下角出现了动漫角色，而且可以调动传感器，让桌面上的 App 图标像是积木一样随着设备角度滑落弹跳。在越狱破解方面，IT之家此前报道，10 月 16 日在巴黎 Hexacon 攻击性安全大会上，安全公司 Calif.io 在一台运行 iOS 27.0.1 系统的 iPhone 18 Pro 机型上，公开演示“完美越狱”，重启后仍可维持最高权限。不过消息源并未明确此次 iPhone Duo 演示是否同样具备重启后保留越狱状态的能力。加州安全研究员斯特凡 · 埃塞尔 (Stefan Esser) 告诉德国网站 Heise，目前不会有面向“最终用户”的越狱工具，但可能会推出概念验证版本。

articles.title: Oncologists Cheer Melanoma Data
articles.content: Leaked data from Moderna and Merck's highly anticipated melanoma vaccine trial has led to a rare disconnect between doctors, who celebrated the result, and Wall Street, which sold off the stocks. Normally results of such pivotal drug studies are binary, with doctors, patients and investors all learning whether a novel medicine will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives and forming the same conclusion. Instead, as reports leaked out on social media about the findings of the melanoma shot — days before the carefully scripted presentation planned for thousands of oncologists gathered in Madrid for the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting — realities diverged. Madison Muller, Bloomberg News Healthcare Reporter, reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 男子醉酒后车机自动报警被判不构成自首：系统可以替你报警但不能替你自首
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，由于把“110”设成紧急联系人，浙江一男子醉驾后，车辆发现异常上报给车企紧急救援中心并自动报警，后续被民警当场查获。该男子显然不服，并辩称这属于自首。那么，这类车机触发的报警，法律上到底能不能认定为自首？据央视《法治在线》今日报道，这类新型醉驾案在法律上不能被认定为自首。车辆紧急救援系统自动拨出的报警电话，不能替驾驶人完成“自动投案”。此次事件发生于 2026 年 3 月 19 日晚，周某酒后驾驶一辆小型普通客车返回家中，途中开启车辆驾驶辅助功能，后因酒劲上头困意难忍而选择在路边停车，随后在驾驶位昏睡起来。但此时车辆仍处于启动状态，车企紧急救援中心监测到车辆长时间无人接管、多次呼叫驾驶人无应答后，按照应急处置流程拨打了周某预设的紧急联系人电话 ——110。民警到场后发现周某身上有明显酒气，经呼气检测及后续血样鉴定，其血液酒精含量为 186mg/100ml，远超 80mg/100ml 的醉驾标准。周某对醉驾事实供认不讳，但又提出车辆自动报警应视为委托投案，且本人始终留在现场未逃离，请求认定为自首。法院没有接受这一逻辑。浙江缙云县人民法院对该案作出判决，认定周某不构成自首，以危险驾驶罪判处拘役一个月，并处罚金 2000 元，一审宣判后周某未上诉，判决已生效。法院指出，根据刑法第六十七条，自首须同时具备自动投案与如实供述两个要件，而“自动投案”的核心在于行为人基于自己的意志，主动、自愿地将自己置于司法机关控制之下。承办法官从主观与客观两个层面拆解了周某的处境：主观上，周某因醉酒昏睡已丧失对车辆的实质管控，车企拨出电话的原因是车辆长时间无人接管、呼叫无回应，目的是排查驾驶人的人身安全风险，并非受周某委托代为投案，周某本人缺乏投案的意识；客观上，周某滞留现场是因为醉酒后无法继续驾车而被动形成的结果，并非主动留在现场等候公安机关处理。技术系统按预设程序执行的报警动作，与行为人自主作出的投案决定，在刑法评价上不能混为一谈。这一认定与最高人民法院此前明确的裁判规则相衔接。2026 年 2 月发布的指导性案例 271 号（王某群危险驾驶案）指出，车载辅助驾驶系统不能代替驾驶人成为驾驶主体，驾驶人激活辅助驾驶功能后仍是实际执行驾驶任务的人，负有确保行车安全的责任；即使驾驶人利用配件逃避系统监测、不在主驾驶位实际操控，仍应作为驾驶主体承担法律责任。同年 3 月，最高人民法院工作报告进一步写入“驾驶人醉酒后启用辅助驾驶功能仍应承担刑事责任”。在上述指导性案例中，王某群血液酒精含量为 114.5mg/100ml，因加装“智驾神器”坐到副驾驶位睡觉，最终被判处拘役一个月十五日、罚金 4000 元。与王某群案相比，周某案的特殊性在于争议焦点从“是否构成危险驾驶罪”前移到了“到案方式能否折抵量刑”—— 辅助驾驶没有免除驾驶人的刑事责任，车辆自动报警也没有替驾驶人创造自首情节。辅助驾驶与自动驾驶之间的责任分界，在这类案件中反复成为前提性问题。依据国家标准《汽车驾驶自动化分级》，L0 至 L2 级均属辅助驾驶，系统仅提供预警或短暂的横纵向控制，驾驶人必须全程监管并随时准备接管，是唯一的责任主体；L3 级有条件自动驾驶是责任主体从驾驶员向车企转移的节点，系统激活期间发生事故，责任指向生产企业。当前市面上绝大多数家用车型搭载的仍是 L2 级系统，这意味着“开启辅助驾驶后放任不管”本身即构成对法定义务的违反。民事层面遵循同一逻辑：因驾驶人分心、疏于接管或违规使用辅助驾驶导致事故，驾驶员承担主要乃至全部责任；只有当鉴定确认车辆存在产品缺陷或功能故障，且与事故存在直接因果关系时，车企才进入赔偿责任的范围。2026 年 10 月北京金融法院联合发布的智能网联汽车保险纠纷报告进一步提出了“对外顺位赔付、对内追偿归属”的双层结构，试图在受害人救济与驾驶人、车企之间的最终责任分配之间作出区分。相关阅读：《男子醉酒后开智驾在超车道停车睡着，被判拘役 1 个月处罚金 2000 元》《一男子醉酒后使用辅助驾驶发生事故并冲卡，被拘役三个月 + 罚款九千元》《奕境曾清林谈“武汉首例醉酒辅助驾驶司机被判刑”：事件本质是醉驾，不是智驾》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，长城汽车今日宣布魏牌二代蓝山全球首秀定档 10 月 27 日。新车采用方盒子设计，搭载由 2.0T 发动机组成的 Hi-4 插电混动系统。据介绍，魏牌二代蓝山主打“东方豪华”，尺寸为 5300×2050×1960mm、轴距 3010mm，轮胎规格 275/50 R21。新车搭载 2.0T 混动专用发动机，匹配 4 挡混动专用变速箱，电机功率为前 110kW、后 220kW，内置 66.6kWh（1/3C）电池。IT之家注意到，官方公布了该车的曜石黑、浅蓝外观配色，新车也已经在工信部完成申报。其尺寸为 5300×2050×1960mm、轴距 3010mm，轮胎规格 275/50 R21。新车正面配备直瀑式镀铬格栅，前大灯是复古风的圆形设计，尾部印有“蓝山”标识，采用平开式尾门，尾灯为双圆形组合，此次公布的影像中，新车用上了大饼轮毂，豪华气息又增加了不少。

articles.title: 国家邮政局召开邮政快递业安全治理规范化座谈会：要持续深入推进“反内卷”工作
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，据国家邮政局，10 月 22 日至 23 日，国家邮政局在河南洛阳召开邮政快递业安全治理规范化座谈会。会议要求，各级邮政管理部门要强化行业监管核心职能，大力加强行业安全监管，维护快递市场秩序。各企业要把安全责任牢牢扛在肩上，统筹发展和安全，进一步抓实抓细行业安全各项工作。会议强调，要聚焦突出问题和关键环节，以更大力度更实举措做好行业安全工作：一是大力整治生产安全突出隐患。要强化重大事故隐患排查整治，深入整治消防隐患，严格规范外包管理，持续完善企业安全管理体系。二是突出抓好寄递渠道风险防范。要抓好寄递安全“三项制度”落实，抓实抓细行业反诈工作，加强寄递物品安全管理，加强信息安全防范。三是强化事前事中事后全链条监管。要加强事前准入与事中事后管理衔接，抓好两项强制性国家标准执行，加强协议用户规范管理，提升广大群众用邮安全感。四是持续深入推进“反内卷”工作。要确保末端派费稳定，深化成本核算指导，严肃整治跨区揽件行为，企业总部要优化对所属服务网络的考核管理规则，不得层层加码、转嫁经营成本。五是加强风险研判，及时化解矛盾纠纷，全力做好行业稳定工作。IT之家注意到，国家邮政局于 10 月 19 日公布 2026 年 1-9 月邮政行业运行情况，整理主要内容如下：1—9 月，邮政行业业务收入（不包括邮政储蓄银行直接营业收入）累计完成 13893.1 亿元，同比增长 5.8%。其中，快递业务收入累计完成 11634.4 亿元，同比增长 7.2%。1—9 月，邮政行业寄递业务量累计完成 1641.3 亿件，同比增长 3.7%。其中，快递业务量累计完成 1513.0 亿件，同比增长 4.3%。

articles.title: OpenAI 联合研究机构部署数千个 AI 智能体：32 分钟分析数百万个小鼠脑细胞，相当于人类数月时间
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，OpenAI 联合 PerturbAI 和斯克里普斯研究所（Scripps Research），利用数千个 AI 智能体分析数百万个小鼠脑细胞的生物学数据，整个分析过程仅耗时 32 分钟。研究团队估计，如果由人类研究人员逐项分析实验结果并检索相关文献，完成同等工作可能需要数月到一年。根据 OpenAI 10 月 21 日发布的介绍，这项研究使用了专为生命科学研究设计的 GPT-Rosalind 模型，分析一份覆盖整个小鼠大脑的 CRISPR 图谱。该图谱记录了不同基因受到干预后，各类脑细胞产生的变化，有助于研究人员了解基因功能及其与疾病之间的潜在联系。研究团队采用分布式 AI 智能体架构，将大量分析任务拆分后并行执行。每个智能体负责研究一种基因干预，分析相关细胞的反应，并检索科学文献，为观察到的变化寻找可能的生物学解释。随后，研究人员将各智能体的报告整合为一份名为“Reasoning Atlas”的推理图谱，关联基因、细胞变化、参考文献和潜在作用机制。研究人员发现，分布式智能体不仅能够复现已有研究中的部分结论，还提出了一些值得进一步验证的线索。例如，Tsc1 和 Tsc2 是共同参与调控细胞生长、代谢等过程的两个基因，但研究发现，在小脑部分神经元中，干预 Tsc2 会改变多种与神经元通信有关的基因表达，而干预 Tsc1 并未产生同等程度的变化。这一差异可能有助于研究人员进一步理解结节性硬化症相关的脑部异常。另一条线索涉及与神经退行性疾病有关的 DCTN1 基因。研究发现，干预该基因后，部分与胆固醇合成有关的基因表达水平上升。AI 智能体将这一现象与既有文献中有关胆固醇运输异常的研究联系起来，并提出一个待验证的问题：DCTN1 功能异常是否会影响神经元内部的胆固醇分布，并进一步参与神经退行性变化。研究团队还对分布式智能体与单个智能体的表现进行了盲测比较。在 20 组配对报告中，生物学专家在 75% 的评审中更倾向于分布式智能体生成的报告；单个智能体的报告获得 16.7% 的评审偏好，其余 8.3% 的评审结果为平局。研究人员称，随着分析任务规模扩大，分布式架构也能检索和引用更多科学文献。在最大规模的测试中，分布式智能体引用了 700 多篇文献，而单个智能体仅引用 11 篇。相关研究论文已于 2026 年 10 月 16 日发布在 bioRxiv 预印本平台，目前尚未经过同行评审。研究团队强调，AI 提出的生物学联系和作用机制仍属于有待验证的研究假设，后续仍需通过实验确认。相关推理图谱、分析流程和代码已向研究人员开放，可用于探索基因干预结果、比较不同细胞类型的反应，并筛选值得优先开展实验的研究方向。IT之家附论文地址：https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.10.15.759436v1相关阅读：《OpenAI 联手 PerturbAI：让近 2000 个 AI 智能体一起搞科研，加速新药研发》

articles.title: 中国科学家在地球深处发现隐藏氧气来源：高压实验显示硅酸盐熔体可储存超 5% 额外氧
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，地球大气中的氧气从何而来，绝大部分人都会说光合作用。但一项新研究提出，在地球历史的某个关键节点，岩浆本身可能也曾充当过重要的氧气搬运工。中国学者发表在《国家科学评论》上的一项高压实验与模拟研究显示，硅酸盐熔体在高压下能够容纳远超传统化学计量预期的“额外氧”，这些氧随岩浆上升、压力降低而被逐步释放，为理解约 25 亿至 20 亿年前大气氧含量的第一次大幅上升提供了一条此前未被纳入考量的深部路径。传统上，地球科学家计算岩浆中的氧含量，依据的是硅、镁、铁等主要元素的丰度和价态。氧在硅酸盐地幔中占原子总数的一半以上，但绝大部分被化学键固定，其数量被认为完全由这些阳离子的“配方”决定。与水和二氧化碳不同，氧本身长期不被视为一种可以独立溶解在岩浆中的挥发性组分。由北京高压科学研究中心（HPSTAR）林彦好研究员与毛河光院士领衔，联合西北工业大学牛海洋教授及阿姆斯特丹自由大学 Wim van Westrenen 教授的团队，对这一默认假设进行了直接检验。研究团队在实验室中合成了洋中脊玄武岩，在 1200 至 1800 摄氏度、1 个大气压至 7 吉帕斯卡的范围内进行熔融实验。7 吉帕斯卡约相当于 100 万磅每平方英寸的压力，接近上地幔的部分条件。为制造富氧环境，他们在部分样品中加入了氧化铂，随后将熔体快速冷却为玻璃，并测量其元素组成、水含量和二氧化碳含量，从中剥离出“化学计量必需氧”与“挥发分中的氧”，剩余部分被定义为“额外氧”。结果呈现出清晰的压强依赖：在 1 个大气压下，额外氧接近于零；当压力升至 7 吉帕斯卡时，额外氧超过了样品重量的 5%，精确值为 5.2 ± 0.2 wt.%。作为对照，未添加氧化铂的同等温压实验仅产出 0.2% 至 0.5 wt.% 的额外氧。一个关键问题是，这些多出来的氧究竟进入了熔体结构，还是仅仅以气泡形式被物理包裹。拉曼光谱检测未在玻璃中发现氧气的气态信号，表明额外氧已被结合进硅酸盐网络之中。牛海洋团队基于深度神经网络原子间势的模拟进一步解释了这一容纳机制：随着氧含量升高，氧原子的电荷分布范围变宽，其中一小部分氧原子彼此之间形成了过氧化物型的键。模拟采用的简化镁-硅-氧体系给出的绝对氧含量低于玄武岩实验，但同样复现了氧储量随压力上升的趋势。由于部分氧可能在淬火过程中逃逸，实验测得的 5% 量级很可能只是熔体实际储存能力的下限。这一发现的意义延伸到地表。在氧化性较强的地幔区域形成的岩浆，可以在深处装载大量额外氧；当它向上运移、压力下降时，熔体的储氧能力随之降低，过剩的氧便会被释放出来，氧化浅部地幔、地壳和大气。研究作者指出，这一机制与地质记录中的一个时间重叠形成了呼应：大气氧含量在约 25 亿至 20 亿年前的大氧化事件（GOE）期间显著上升，而一些规模最大的大火成岩省（LIPs）也恰好在相近的时间窗口大规模喷发。基于实验数据的粗略估算显示，如果那一时期喷发的岩浆仅释放出其重量 0.27% 的额外氧，就足以供应今天整个大气层中所含的氧气总量。这一数字与实验在 7 吉帕斯卡下测得的储氧能力相比并不苛刻，但需要注意的是，0.27% 是基于全球规模岩浆活动的量级推演，并非对某一次具体喷发的直接测量，其与实际地质过程的吻合程度仍有待后续工作检验。IT之家附论文地址：https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag539

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，比亚迪今日发布了第二代海豹 07 内饰官图，新车采用了全新设计语言，除了保留大尺寸悬浮中控屏和液晶仪表外，方向盘、中控台装饰、出风口造型均有所变化。据介绍，该车搭载奢享舒适座椅，支持零重力、按摩、通风、加热等功能，拥有同级最大后排空间，配备 20 扬帝瓦雷音响。此前，比亚迪汽车海洋网销售事业部总经理张卓已公布第二代海豹 07 的外观，新车的定位将是 C 级全享家轿。相比现款车型，新车前脸拥有大量锋利的线条，采用全新样式的日行灯组，显得更加“凶猛”；侧面则采用类似溜背的轮廓，张力十足。细节方面，新车还配备半隐藏式门把手和车顶激光雷达。IT之家注意到，新车已于 8 月登陆工信部申报名单，车身尺寸为长 5080mm /宽 1960mm /高 1495mm，轴距达到 2960mm，额定载客 5 人，提供纯电、插混两种动力版本可选。纯电版本搭载由西安比亚迪汽车零部件有限公司生产的永磁同步驱动电机，提供两种动力版本：低功率版本峰值功率 245kW，额定功率 115kW，整备质量 1975kg；高功率版本峰值功率 300kW，额定功率 150kW，整备质量 2060kg。纯电车型电池均采用磷酸铁锂蓄电池，由弗迪电池相关企业生产，最高车速可达 240km/h。

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level validation losses and gameplay benchmarks from in-corpus worlds to unseen worlds. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-driven evolutionary search is a promising paradigm for scientific discovery, but existing methods remain costly and slow, often applying expensive reasoning uniformly while underusing evidence from failed, redundant, and saturated trials. We introduce Speculative Evolution (SpecEvo), a multi-LLM framework that coordinates lightweight and frontier models through continual consolidation of search evidence. Lightweight models power both parallel Speculators, which generate and refine candidate programs, and an Advisor, which distills accumulated successes, failures, and saturated directions into persistent guidance for subsequent exploration. At sparse checkpoints, a frontier-model Navigator inspects the evolving population and intervenes through synthesis, surgical refinement, or reframing according to search stagnation. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28763v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. We introduce Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed for measuring how far today's agents can improve the published best models on scientific ML benchmarks, spanning 20 benchmarks across 11 domains. Rather than ranking agents on a leaderboard, Agent4Sci asks what kinds of progress agents can make on these tasks under in-the-wild conditions, and where they fall short. Empirically, today's frontier agents advance the published best on every benchmark, with Claude Opus reaching 10.4% mean relative improvement and no run flagged for academic misconduct. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28815v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic harness evolution optimizes an agent's instructions, tools, and control flow by using its task execution experiences as evolving evidence. While more evolution tasks should intuitively improve performance, our preliminary study reveals a paradoxical failure mode: the performance of existing methods degrades as the task pool expands. Our further analysis demonstrates that this degradation stems from suboptimal evidence selection during optimization, as different evidence combinations lead to substantially different evolution outcomes. To address this issue, we propose Successive Scale Racing (SSR), a framework that adaptively searches for optimal evidence combinations in each evolution round. SSR constructs diverse evidence combinations based on the corresponding task quality and coverage, and efficiently races the resulting candidate harnesses under a small compute budget. articles.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28826v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale. We compared Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, with frontier and open-weight LLM judges in four use cases. On 118 pediatric answers, Jev's agreement with physicians' ordinal quality ratings (Gwet's AC2 0.50; expected score 0.53) matched or exceeded that of seven of 12 LLM judges, including frontier models, Claude Opus 5.5 (0.49) and GPT-6 (0.38). On physician-graded binary HealthBench criteria, Jev matched or exceeded four of six LLM judges. On MedHELM's open-ended tasks, Jev's agreement with a three-LLM jury approached or exceeded the jurors' internal agreement. On HealthBench Professional, Jev matched the benchmark's reference judge, GPT-5.4, on 91% of criteria (other judges, 91-93%). Frontier judges cost 73-294 times more than Jev and took 7-57 times longer.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Progress on foundation model pretraining is gated by who can afford a trial, and relational pretraining is no exception. Recipes are developed inside individual labs, reported under private protocols, and do not accumulate. Speedrun leaderboards remove that barrier by decentralizing the search rather than the training run. The problem is fixed, the stack is open, entries are ranked by wall-clock time to a quality target, and one GPU is enough to hold the record. We introduce modded-nanoRT, the first such leaderboard for Relational Transformers. Which database to hold out decides whether the benchmark can resolve improvements at all, so we fix it by calibration, ranking six candidates by how sharply a 45-minute learning curve separates improvement from seed noise. Abstract: Large language models increasingly take part in extended conversations where they can both shape and be shaped by another party's views, yet most persuasion research measures only one side of that exchange. We introduce a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework in which two language-model roles repeatedly discuss a contested topic (climate-change attribution): one is given an assigned stance and, in some conditions, an explicit instruction to persuade, while the other receives no assigned position. Opinion dynamics differ substantially across model combinations: same-model interactions narrow the opinion gap on average, clearly for only one of the two models, while cross-model interactions widen it. Abstract: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. We introduce Fig (Finding Interactions in Games), an agentic system that performs targeted elicitation interventions on game environments. It takes a natural language behavior description, decomposes it into sub-behaviors, generates new social games or selects existing ones, and executes single or combined interventions to the games' engine, opponents, instructions, and context. Abstract: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28909v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing. We present DiffResearch, an open multi-agent deep research framework that places a diffusion language model (dLLM) at the core of every stage, and measure how a diffusion backbone changes latency and report quality. Holding the agentic scaffold, retrieval code, prompts, and evaluation fixed, we swap the backbone between an open diffusion model and a comparable AR model. Across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks, the diffusion backbone is roughly 6 times faster end-to-end, driven by order-of-magnitude reductions in planning and writing. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28914v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier language-model agents excel at complex tasks, but high inference costs make transferring their capabilities to smaller models essential. Traditional knowledge distillation achieves this through parameter updates, requiring access to the student's weights and additional training compute while encoding the transferred knowledge implicitly in the parameters. We introduce D-Skill, a framework that treats the teacher as a black box and distills its behavioral advantage into an interpretable natural-language skill by analyzing paired rollouts and identifying behavioral divergences and agreements. The resulting lessons are consolidated offline, with any compatible skill-update backend, into a skill document that is provided to the student at inference time. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents now complete tasks autonomously, modifying real-world state such as artifacts, software environments, and configurations along the way. Yet they show limited backup awareness: recognizing that an action will modify state that may later be needed, and preserving it beforehand. To evaluate backup awareness, we introduce RegretBench, a benchmark of 205 executable tasks grounded in regret moments reported on platforms such as X.com, GitHub, and Stack Overflow, where users explicitly regretted not preserving state they later needed. Across six frontier models, agents complete 86.1% of tasks on average yet back up before these moments in only 15.2%, showing that task completion ability does not imply backup awareness. Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly expected to interact with environments and improve their decisions during deployment. We propose a test-time framework, inspired by Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control, that combines multi-branch predictive analysis with experience-based adaptation. At each step, the agent proposes multiple candidate actions and imagines their outcomes with a world model, so that alternatives can be compared without being executed in the environment. Abstract: While large language models are increasingly deployed as tool-calling agents, their safety evaluations still focus primarily on their ability to refuse harmful requests in text. We construct a benchmark of 2,304 prompts across four domains, consisting of matched triplets that present the same harmful or benign request in text-only, standard tool-enabled, and adversarially framed tool-enabled settings. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28987v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. We present PerMIT, a memory architecture with provable integrity guarantees under an explicit trust assumption: only user-typed inputs and values confirmed at a gate are trusted. PerMIT mediates the release and use of untrusted environment-derived values through a finite memory interface, while preserving agent-driven multi-turn planning and tool choice. Abstract: Customized agent deployments define policies over tools, resources, and execution conditions. Providing these policies in the task agent's prompt does not reliably prevent violations. arXiv:2610.30206v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models scale model capacity efficiently by activating a small subset of parameters per token. However, in long-context inference, memory remains a major bottleneck because the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length. Existing KV cache compression methods reduce this cost for dense transformers, but overlook a problem specific to MoE: KV eviction can change which experts are selected during answer generation, degrading the generation quality. We propose MoEZip, a routing-aware KV cache compression for sparse MoE language models. To estimate the sensitivity of expert routing to perturbation, we propose a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions. MoEZip combines this metric with attention weights for routing-aware scoring of contexts. Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in competitive programming, and their outputs are sensitive to how a prompt is phrased. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30225v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. articles.title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. Training choices changed how many patients had high attack scores, but the patients who ranked highest by risk largely stayed the same across the configurations we tested. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual mathematical reasoning can fail before reasoning begins: when a vision-language model (VLM) misreads a diagram, subsequent reasoning proceeds from false premises. This perceptual bottleneck is especially pronounced in smaller models, while accurate textual descriptions can substantially narrow the gap to larger models. Because obtaining such descriptions at inference requires additional annotation or model calls, we propose minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation. Using reference figure descriptions and verified reference solutions as training-only information, a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective, and only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss. Correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning. This preserves on-policy supervision while avoiding full-response imitation. Abstract: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. We study PolarGD, the orthogonalized update at the core of Muon, on matrix quadratics, where optimizers can be analyzed in closed form, and compare update directions under line search to remove the effect of learning-rate tuning. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents spend substantial computation generating actions and processing long interaction histories. Poor action choices can steer agents into low-value states, wasting computation and increasing API costs. Sampling and verifying alternative actions can improve the agent's decisions, but applying this procedure at every step adds substantial overhead. We introduce SWE-Verifier, a lightweight generative model that selectively triggers candidate sampling and verification. It scores the coding agent's proposed action to determine when additional candidate sampling is needed, then ranks the resulting actions before execution. We train SWE-Verifier from Qwen3.5-4B using preference data that groups contrasting actions with their resulting environment observations and rubric-guided teacher scores. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30291v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A fundamental challenge in Bayesian network structure learning lies in efficiently approximating the posterior distribution of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). For large, high-dimensional datasets, the task remains beyond the capabilities of current methods. This work advances Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms by introducing novel moves that simultaneously resample the parents for multiple nodes of the DAG. At the core of these moves is duet sampling, a new generalization of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm that selects two proposal distributions from a pool at each iteration. One is used for generating a candidate state of the Markov chain and another for evaluating the return to the current state; both are ingredients of an appropriately crafted acceptance criterion. The Generator learns a distribution of continuous reference solutions using data from numerical simulations or experimental measurements to represent a target physical regime. Abstract: In recent years, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have gained massive attention as an energy-efficient neural computing paradigm due to their event-driven and sparse computing capability. However, maintaining accuracy under low-precision constraints, necessary for practical deployment, has been largely unexplored for SNN models. In addition, existing Hessian-based approaches for quantization, such as HAWQ-V2, incur significant memory and computational overhead due to temporal unrolling across multiple SNN timesteps. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon node outages are harder than conventional missing-value imputation because complete sensor trajectories remain unobserved for extended periods, while the usefulness of spatial and temporal dependencies varies across outage locations and operating regimes. Existing graph, diffusion, and flow-based methods typically impose a fixed structural bias, which can oversmooth abrupt changes or propagate errors from unreliable neighbors. We introduce CTRL-FM, an observation-preserving flow-matching framework that treats structural guidance as an outage-conditioned inference-time decision. A missing-only flow-matching backbone learns a conditional velocity field while keeping observed measurements exactly fixed. Abstract: Activation probes are computed directions in a language model's residual stream, used both to detect safety-relevant behaviours and, by adding their direction back into the stream, to steer them. Abstract: We study the Bayesian fixed-confidence best-arm identification problem in which a learner can abstain from making a terminal recommendation. Abstract: Protein classifiers are highly sensitive to evaluation protocol: random train/test splits induce phylogenetic leakage, allowing models to exploit taxon-specific correlations and substantially overestimate out-of-distribution performance. This issue is particularly acute for venom compound classification by ion-channel target (Ca2+, K+, Na+), where reported accuracies of 80-90% do not reflect generalization to unseen taxa. Current methods limit the design space by imposing differentiable soft manufacturability loss penalties, or by fixing structures through post-processing, causing a discrepancy between the geometry optimized by the physics model and the final fabricated result. Thus, we present AcoustiPrint, a physics-informed neural architecture for constrained inverse design that represents three-dimensional geometries with an implicit neural representation (INR) and passes each candidate through a printability operator before evaluating its final response. Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), as a decision-support aid, provides new tools for studying history effectively using multimodal data, including text, images, and audio. Abstract: Many Indian banks serve customers through FAQ pages and scripted chatbots. Assistants based on language models could respond faster and carry out requests such as blocking a card, but only if they give correct information and follow the bank's rules. These rules prescribe a procedure, a set of required steps, such as obtaining a closure quote before closing a deposit. Adapting models to this domain requires measuring how well they follow the procedure, before and after training. Benchmarks usually judge only the records left at the end of a conversation. Many required steps, however, leave the records unchanged, so an assistant that skips them can still be judged successful. Abstract: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. Abstract: Hallucinated citations make it harder to trace sources and verify the evidence behind scientific claims. Detecting them is difficult because bibliographic records can be incomplete or differ across source types and publication versions. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer factual questions, but their answers can contain errors and must be fact-checked claim by claim. Abstract: LLM judges are used to determine which of two answers is better. Trusting these verdicts requires knowing how repeatable they are and how much they depend on the judge's instructions. Using 500 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts with two models' answers held fixed, we run GPT-4.1 as the judge under all eight combinations of criteria, output format and task framing, and repeat every setup unchanged at temperature zero on a pinned model version. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Protegrity-PII, a new PII decision model for structured and unstructured text. Protegrity-PII achieves a typed recall of 0.915 with a precision of 0.907 on a new benchmark we propose, PII-SCOPE. Our model processes text in 0.49 seconds per million characters at \$0.0005 per million characters on a single RTX 6000 using batched inference. Due in part to the expansive nature of the entity type taxonomy used in training, Protegrity-PII achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization when benchmarked against a selection of state of the art models and datasets.

Abstract: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), the standard for building information exchange in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), is increasingly queried through large language models (LLMs) using natural language. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding-agent benchmarks often describe a task in natural language but grade it with tests taken from the upstream project. Passing those tests can require information the description never states: a constant's name, a module path, an exact message. We call this a specification-oracle gap: where it exists, a benchmark also measures whether an agent reproduces upstream implementation details. We formalise the gap, including the inconsistencies that chains of dependent tasks add, and build a static audit for five languages that classifies every name-, path- and literal-level dependency of every scored test (held-out precision 89.2%, recall 92.9%). On SWE-Milestone (98 graded milestones, 35 published runs), 25 milestones contain a test that depends on an unstated, non-inferable name or path. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30664v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. Abstract: Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored. articles.title: WikiOriginQA: Automated Construction of a QA Dataset with Knowledge Origins for Analyzing Cultural Bias
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30677v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing datasets on cultural knowledge have been typically created by human annotators familiar with each culture. However, the process requires considerable human effort, presenting a significant challenge to scalability. To address this challenge, we introduce WikiOriginQA, a QA dataset automatically constructed by objectively representing the origins of knowledge through the creation dates of different Wikipedia language editions. Experimental results with the created dataset confirm that LLM performance tends to be biased toward Anglophone cultures. Furthermore, the results suggest the importance of knowledge propagation into the Anglosphere. These findings demonstrate the validity of our automated approach, enabling cultural bias evaluations with superior scalability across diverse languages without extensive manual annotation.

Abstract: We study mountain-bike action quality assessment (AQA) with weak labels and candidate feedback. Abstract: We introduce EgoHand, a monocular 3D hand reconstruction model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on egocentric video. Central to our approach is the curation of a high-quality training corpus of 14 million images, combining synthetic data, in-the-wild video, and multi-camera motion capture to balance scene diversity and supervision quality. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30337v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. Abstract: We introduce Foundation4D, a unified feed-forward model for geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera driving video. Our video inference pipeline uses pose graph optimization to refine camera trajectories and assembles object tracks across input windows. We also develop a data annotation pipeline and release PAI-Foundation4D, a benchmark with dense depth and semantic occupancy labels for 1,253 driving clips. With benchmark-specific fine-tuning, Foundation4D achieves the lowest depth AbsRel on Waymo and nuScenes, the highest detection mAP on nuScenes, and the highest occupancy mIoU on OpenOccupancy among the compared methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30347v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose FiLM-CAM; a conditional-access image watermarking approach that enforces authorized encoding, decoding, and removal through keyed feature modulation. A secret key conditions a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism that transforms the internal representation of the watermark signal before embedding, thereby coupling the payload to the key at the feature, rather than pixel level. The same key must be presented to condition the decoder to correctly recover the payload embedded in an image. To enforce conditional access, we train the system to maximize the performance gap between authorized and unauthorized use, ensuring reliable extraction under the correct key while inducing failure under incorrect keys. In addition, we design our encoder to estimate the watermark residual invariant to the presence of pre-existing watermarks. articles.title: Latent Space Jam: Layout Guided Video Synthesis
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adding control to video generation often requires training, which demands additional computational resources, data, or architectural changes. We propose a training-free approach that utilizes pretrained video diffusion models to control object layout and motion using coarse layouts. Our method operates in two passes: first, it steers spatiotemporal placement through prompt-guided cross-attention to produce a coarse visual guide; second, this guide conditions the same model to generate a high-quality, layoutconsistent video. The approach enables coordinated motion with strong temporal consistency, supporting diverse trajectories and object interactions without additional training. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently outperforms prior work in overlap and trajectory accuracy, as well as visual quality across static, dynamic, and multi-object scene settings.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30405v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern vision-based agents have shifted toward skill-based problem-solving, where a skill is an executable image-to-image operation, e.g., cropping, thresholding, or edge detection. As these skill libraries grow, they accumulate duplicated, mislabeled, and defective skills. The signals normally used to curate them (a skill's name, description, or source code) say little about how the skill visually changes the image. We present VisCurate, a framework and benchmark that curates visual skill libraries from observed execution rather than from text. VisCurate runs each candidate skill pair on a shared probe battery and assigns one of six behavioral relations, each tied to a library edit that is safe to make. The benchmark injects seven defect types into a clean library at controlled rates, producing 300 reproducible instances with ground-truth relations and repairs. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30468v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducing a published 3DGS paper takes weeks of expert engineering before any extension can be proposed. Prior autonomous-research systems read papers, draft hypotheses, and write code, but are limited by short fixed templates, low executability, and weak traceability, and none has been demonstrated end-to-end in a live computer-vision subfield with intense activity. SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that addresses these limitations. Given a research prompt, a target-paper URL, or no input at all, it reproduces a published baseline, proposes an extension, trains and ablates across Mip-NeRF 360 and LLFF, writes the manuscript, and binds every reported number to a logged training run. Abstract: Self-supervised Vision Transformers learn strong image-level representations, but their patch-level representations can be unreliable for dense prediction. articles.title: Asking Less, Adapting Better: Feedback-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-and-Language Navigation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow instructions and navigate to target locations. However, current VLN agents often suffer severe performance degradation in unseen environments due to distribution shifts. Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising paradigm to bridge this gap, yet existing methods that rely on unsupervised entropy minimization can propagate errors through the trajectory, causing cascading failures in navigation. Recent methods mitigate this by incorporating human feedback, but they apply trajectory-level supervision uniformly across all steps without localizing the actions is truly informative, leading to inefficient feedback utilization and mismatched optimization granularity. Abstract: Federated unsupervised domain adaptation (FUDA) addresses the challenge of adapting models to an unlabeled target domain using decentralized source domains while preserving data privacy. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into embodied robotic planning, yet standard benchmarks primarily evaluate end-to-end task completion in nominal environments, obscuring failure origins across the execution stack. We present Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation. Alpha injects calibrated faults across perception (sensor lag), actuation (grip slip), kinematics (unreachable targets), and planning (planner-output corruption), alongside concurrent conditions. To separate physical vulnerabilities from planner sensitivities, we introduce a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria. Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks and real-world deployments. Self-play in vectorized simulators changes the economics: at millions of rollout steps per second, one can obtain a state distribution with natural diversity in collisions, near-misses, and recoveries that no driving log contains, and a highly reactive policy emerges from a basic driving-quality reward. Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30334v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Designing and tuning reward functions remains one of the main challenges in building effective reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines for humanoid locomotion. While shaping rewards can accelerate learning, naively formulated terms often conflict with the desired behavior, overfit to a specific robot, or become unstable under small weight changes. Potential-Based Reward Shaping (PBRS) offers an alternative solution: shaping the reward via differences of a potential function to guide exploration without changing the optimal policy. In this paper, we study Multi-PBRS for humanoid locomotion and propose a unified reward configuration. We then evaluate the same reward structure and weights across nine humanoid robots, requiring only robot-specific metadata (joint/link mappings and default poses) rather than per-robot reward redesign. Abstract: This paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, combining advanced longitudinal and lateral control strategies to address the challenges of safe and efficient autonomous driving. A novel proof of string stability for the proposed longitudinal control algorithm, based on a PID framework, ensures robust inter-vehicle distance regulation even under dynamic operating conditions. Additionally, an arc-length-based longitudinal error formulation enhances the applicability of the control system for curved roads, making it realistic for diverse driving scenarios. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This paper reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing, and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. articles.title: Integrated Respiratory Sensing and Gated Control for Autonomous Needle Insertion Via CT Bore Robotic Arm
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30452v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Currently, CT-guided lung biopsy is a highly manual procedure requiring patient breath-holding, iterative manual needle insertions, and repeated CT confirmation scans to accurately target a tumor. Automating this process within the CT bore--without relying on manual needle placement or patient breath-holding--has the potential to reduce procedure time, patient discomfort, and radiation exposure. In this work, we present an integrated sensing and control system capable of performing a gated needle insertion within the CT bore. The experiments demonstrate the system's ability to track and predict patient breath cycles, perform autonomous respiratory-gated needle insertion, and detect breath cycle anomalies.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30500v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Motion Diffusion Models (MDMs) can generate diverse and visually appealing human motion; yet, the resulting trajectories frequently violate physical constraints, limiting their downstream use in simulation and control. We present PhysibleMDM, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model. We introduce a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation. These constraints combine kinematic checks (e.g., ground penetration, slip, and self-collision) with dynamic feasibility tests computed via an inverse-dynamics inner loop formulated as a cone program. Abstract: Predicting surrounding vehicles' lane-change intentions enables autonomous vehicles to anticipate potential hazards and respond proactively rather than relying solely on reactive maneuvers. This study investigates the benefits of integrating lane-change prediction, based on knowledge graph embeddings and Bayesian inference, into autonomous vehicle decision-making. Three driving strategies are evaluated in risky merging scenarios simulated in CARLA: reactive driving, prediction-based longitudinal action, and prediction-based lateral action. The proposed prediction model anticipates the surrounding vehicle's lane change approximately 3-4 seconds before its occurrence, allowing the ego vehicle to adjust its behavior accordingly. Abstract: Human motion retargeting bridges the embodiment gap between humans and humanoid robots by converting human demonstrations into reference trajectories for whole-body control and loco-manipulation. For object-interaction tasks, successful execution depends on accurately preserving body--object relations at critical stages. However, uniform per-frame iteration budgets do not account for these localized accuracy requirements, limiting the computational efficiency of retargeting. To address this limitation, we present Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which uses keyframes and key body parts to allocate optimization effort. Specifically, a vision-language model selects relevant motion signals and body parts, and keyframes are identified from changes in the selected signals. Abstract: Recent advances in foundation-model agents have enabled increasingly capable embodied systems for long-horizon planning and interaction. Deploying strong cloud agents leaves the platform idle for seconds between consecutive actions, while lightweight local models respond quickly but are more vulnerable to errors. Existing hierarchical architectures typically assign models fixed roles, whereas conventional model routers make stateless per-request decisions. We present CARE, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate control from a local executor to a stronger cloud model. They also struggle to relocalize objects after scene changes. To address these challenges, we propose the Online Anchor-centric Scene Inference System (OASIS), a unified system for online mapping, complex open-vocabulary retrieval, and navigation in dynamic environments. articles.content:

Abstract: Motion planning is central to robotics, and it is increasingly used to correct the motions proposed by learned planners and policies. In both uses, constraints must hold at every instant of the motion, not only at sampled times. To our knowledge, no algorithm provably converges to a globally optimal motion once a smoothness cost is combined with such constraints. We cast planning and steering as a single continuous-time program: robots avoid one another and static or moving obstacles, and a learned proposal is steered by keeping the motion close to it. The program is elementary to state, yet nonconvex. We propose GlobMP (Global Motion Planning), a gradient projection method over piecewise-polynomial curves, on which each constraint is one polynomial per piece that must stay nonnegative over the whole motion; it alternates cost reduction with feasibility restoration. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual Language Action (VLA) models are designed to be generalist robot models that can be implemented across embodiments, tasks and environments. However, their ability to collaborate with other robots and humans remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a framework to automate the generation of multi-robot collaborative data for decentralized VLA training without requiring human teleoperation. Our framework first utilizes a decentralized collaborative planning approach to generate multi-robot collaborative robot plans in the form of an executable function. We then utilize the collaborative plan to produce collaborative demonstration data to finetune VLA models in a decentralized manner. We show that our approach produces demonstration data that when used to finetune VLA models on decentralized collaboration tasks matches the task performance of VLA models finetuned on human-teleoperated collaborative data.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30735v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow matching is now the dominant approach for vision-language action (VLA) robot policies, thanks to its expressiveness and simple training objective. However, inference for standard flow matching requires iteratively solving an ODE, limiting the control frequency at deployment. While several works have proposed novel methods to allow for single-shot action generation, we ask whether such additional objectives are actually necessary. We find that across six flow matching VLAs, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step sampling at scale: multi-step integration confers little to no consistent advantage at inference. We empirically find that this holds as long as models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity. articles.title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
articles.content: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control. In this paper, we introduce FlexPart, a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that supports variable-granularity geometric conditions within a single model. By seamlessly integrating heterogeneous inputs, ranging from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, via gated adaptive modulation, FlexPart unlocks a powerful cross-modal synergy. We also propose an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism that leverages strong spatial priors to align representations across granularities, improving geometric consistency and facilitating inter-task synergy. Under mask conditioning on PartVerseXL, FlexPart reduces Part CD by 16.6% relative to TripoSG + SAM3D and by 10.5% relative to OmniPart, while maintaining competitive whole-mesh quality. The code can be found at https://github.com/Gucci233/FlexPart

articles.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
articles.content: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

articles.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
articles.content: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

articles.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
articles.content: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

articles.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
articles.content: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

articles.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
articles.content: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.

articles.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
articles.content: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io

articles.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
articles.content: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.

articles.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
articles.content: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

articles.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to train agents that adapt quickly to unseen tasks from limited interaction, but this requires representing task evidence over long interaction histories. Classical recurrent agents compress experience into hidden states, while transformer-based agents retrieve from past trajectories at quadratic memory and computation cost. In this work, we propose Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation (METTA) for meta-reinforcement learning. It decomposes the fast adaptation phase into two temporal scales: a causal neural memory performs fine-grained within-episode adaptation with linear sequence complexity, while compact episode-level summaries support long-range cross-episode task inference without attending over the full interaction history. Moreover, equipping agents with neural memory provides sufficient expressive capacity and test-time training capability, enabling effective adaptation to unseen held-out tasks and task families at meta-test time. On unseen held-out Meta-World ML10/45 test environments, METTA achieves a success rate over $50\%$ while maintaining a low training budget and short wall-clock time. On long-context sparse-reward PointMaze tasks, it outperforms transformer-based baselines by exhibiting more structured exploration behavior. These results show that METTA provides an efficient path toward more adaptive and scalable long-context meta-RL.

articles.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
articles.content: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: https://avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright/
